Working from the article text provided directly.

---

**Published online:**
September 8, 2026 (Reuters, Orlando, Florida dateline)

**Geographic focus:**
United States

**Temporal focus:**
T1. Historical report [YES] — References post-GFC decade, 100-year Treasury return data, pre/post-Feb 28 yield moves
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — Rate hike expectations (~3 hikes by mid-next year), war/energy shock resolution scenarios
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — Widening deficit trajectory, AI borrowing binge, inflation expectations becoming unmoored, structurally elevated yields

**Synopsis:**
The article argues the US bond market, despite negative sentiment around $40T debt, 6% deficit-to-GDP, and ~5% 10Y yields, is functioning normally and rationally. Yields reflect strong nominal growth (~6%), persistent above-target inflation (nearly 6 years above 2%), and a near-full-employment labor market. Volatility (MOVE index) remains subdued, and foreign central bank reallocation has been gradual. JPMorgan views current yields as fair or even slightly low. The article identifies the Feb 28 US-Israel attack on Iran as a key inflection point, driving ~100bps rise in 2Y yields and a full reversal in Fed expectations from ~3 cuts to ~3 hikes. It concludes yields will remain structurally elevated but are a feature, not a bug, of a properly functioning market.

---

**Q01. Is the content's main message on the US economy, US yields, US interest rates?**
Relevance: YES — Core thesis is that elevated US yields and the bond market's behavior are consistent with macro fundamentals (growth, inflation, deficit, Fed policy).

**Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?**
Relevance: 75 (moderately-high — rate hike expectations are a central forward-looking element; Fed has pivoted from ~3 cuts to ~3 hikes by mid-next year)
Probability of increase: 65%

**Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?**
Relevance: 20 (low — stability is not the primary frame; the direction has shifted meaningfully hawkish)
Probability of holding: 15%

**Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?**
Relevance: 15 (low — cuts are mentioned only as the prior consensus that has now been fully reversed; a geopolitical resolution could partially revive this narrative)
Probability of decrease: 20%

**Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?**
Sentiment: +60 (Hawkish — Fed expectations have fully flipped to ~3 hikes by mid-next year, 2Y yields up 100bps since Feb 28, inflation persistently above target, deficit widening, AI borrowing adding supply pressure; tempered slightly by the author's view that yields are fair/rational rather than alarming, and that a geopolitical resolution could reverse some of the move)
